issues.description: Email validation regex is too simplistic and doesn't follow RFC 5322 standards. The pattern /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ will accept invalid emails like 'a@b.c' and reject valid ones with subdomains.
issues.suggestion: Consider using a more robust email validation approach. For production, use a library like 'email-validator' or implement RFC 5322 compliant regex. At minimum, verify the email through a confirmation link.

issues.description: HTML entity encoding is performed manually with multiple replace() calls, which is repetitive and error-prone. This approach may miss other dangerous characters in certain contexts.
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested library like 'he' or 'xss' to handle HTML escaping. These libraries handle edge cases and are more maintainable.

issues.description: Input validation checks for falsy values but email could be an empty string or whitespace-only string that passes the check. The name validation is similarly weak.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit trim() checks and validate string length: if (!input.email?.trim() || !input.name?.trim()) throw new Error(...)

issues.description: Using Math.random() for ID generation in production is not cryptographically secure or guaranteed unique across concurrent requests. The timestamp-based approach could have collisions under load.
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() or a library like 'nanoid' for secure, unique ID generation. For database primary keys, consider UUIDs or database-generated sequences.

issues.description: Database query and params are defined but the actual execution is commented out, making it unclear if the code has been properly tested or is incomplete.
issues.suggestion: Either implement the actual database call or clearly document why it's commented out. For this fixture file, consider removing the commented code and adding a note.

issues.description: The sanitizeInput function is called only on the name field, but the email field (which comes from user input) is not sanitized before database storage, though it is validated.
issues.suggestion: Consider whether email should also be sanitized consistently, or document why only name requires sanitization. Email validation may be sufficient, but be explicit about the security model.

issues.description: Email is converted to lowercase, which is good for consistency, but should be validated before normalization to provide clearer error messages.
issues.suggestion: Reorder validations: validate first (before normalization), then normalize. This provides better error messages and clearer intent.

codeQuality.summary: The code demonstrates good security awareness with input validation and sanitization practices, but has moderate issues with weak email validation regex, simplistic HTML escaping, weak input checking for empty/whitespace strings, and non-cryptographic ID generation. Best-practice improvements in error handling, library usage, and input validation order would increase code quality to production-ready levels.
